name: Neurological Channelopathy of the Central Nervous System Due to a Genetic Calcium Channel Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in calcium channel genes (e.g., CACNA1A, CACNA1C)
Presence of episodic neurological symptoms such as paroxysmal ataxia, episodic hemiplegia, or migraine with aura
Exclusion of alternative causes by neuroimaging and metabolic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic genetic variant plus presence of characteristic episodic neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing combined with clinical presentation; neuroimaging is typically normal or nonspecific.

pathognomonic.notes: Sudden onset of coordination loss during attacks
Visual or sensory disturbances preceding headache

common.notes: Slurred or scanning speech during or between attacks
Involuntary eye movements observed during episodes
Generalized or focal weakness during attacks

occasional.notes: Focal or generalized seizures in some patients

rare.notes: Observed in advanced or chronic cases
searchTerms: loss of coordination area in brain

rare.notes: Rare involvement due to calcium channel dysfunction
Mood disorders or anxiety in some patients

imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or mild cerebellar atrophy in chronic cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CACNA1A, CACNA1C, or related calcium channel genes
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) may show nonspecific abnormalities during attacks

distinguishingFeatures: Also caused by CACNA1A mutations but with distinct episodic ataxia phenotype
Typically absence of migraine with aura
Prominent migraine with aura and hemiplegia
May overlap genetically but clinical presentation differs
Lactic acidosis and muscle biopsy findings

redFlags: Sudden onset of hemiplegia mimicking stroke
Progressive cerebellar signs with atrophy on imaging
references: Ophoff RA et al. Genetic and clinical aspects of calcium channelopathies. Neurology. 2022.
Orphanet Report Series: Neurological Channelopathies. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2023.
Jen JC et al. Calcium channel mutations in neurological disorders. Nat Rev Neurol. 2021.
